recipes.title: Bulgogi (Marinated Grilled Beef)
recipes.dish_alt: Sliced bulgogi beef with onions and scallions on a plate
recipes.prep_alt: Marinated beef and onions grilling on a Korean barbecue grill

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef ribeye or sirloin, thinly sliced

sections.heading: Steps
items: If the beef isn't pre-sliced, freeze it 20-30 minutes first so it firms up and slices paper-thin.
Grate the Asian pear into a bowl — it adds sweetness and its enzymes gently tenderize the beef.
Stir in the soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and black pepper until the sugar dissolves.
Add the sliced beef and coat every piece in the marinade.
Cover and marinate at least 1 hour in the fridge — overnight is even better.
Heat a large pan or grill pan over medium-high with a little oil until shimmering.
Add the sliced onion and cook 1 minute until just softened and translucent.
Add the beef in a single layer (cook in batches if crowded) and sear 2-3 minutes without moving it.
Flip and cook 1-2 minutes more, until every piece is deep brown with no pink left.
Stir in the scallion pieces for the last 30 seconds, then serve over rice topped with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: Bubbling red kimchi jjigae stew with tofu and pork in a pot
recipes.prep_alt: Kimchi and pork simmering together in a hot pot

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the sesame oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the pork belly 2-3 minutes until the edges turn golden.
Add the chopped kimchi and cook 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant instead of raw-smelling.
Stir in the gochugaru and gochujang, coating the kimchi and pork.
Pour in the water and kimchi brine, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce to a simmer, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and cook 10 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic, and simmer 3 more minutes until the onion softens.
Gently slide in the tofu cubes and simmer 2 more minutes, stirring carefully.
Taste and add a splash more kimchi brine if it needs more depth.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle scallion on top, and serve bubbling hot with rice.

recipes.title: Japchae (Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
recipes.dish_alt: Glossy japchae glass noodles tossed with beef and vegetables
recipes.prep_alt: Sweet potato glass noodles stir-frying with vegetables and pork in a pan

sections.heading: Steps
items: Boil the glass noodles 6-8 minutes until soft, stretchy, and translucent, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Snip the noodles a few times with kitchen scissors so they're easier to eat.
Mix the soy sauce and sugar together, toss two-thirds of it with the noodles and 1 tsp sesame oil, and set aside.
Sear the beef strips in a hot pan 2-3 minutes until no pink remains, then set aside.
In the same pan, cook the onion, carrot, and shiitake 3-4 minutes until the carrot still has a little crunch.
Add the spinach and stir just until wilted, about 1 minute.
Return the beef and noodles to the pan with the rest of the soy-sugar mix, tossing 1-2 minutes until golden.
Off heat, drizzle in the remaining sesame oil and toss once more.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Doenjang Jjigae (Soybean Paste Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: Hearty doenjang jjigae stew with tofu, potato, and zucchini
recipes.prep_alt: A bowl of fermented doenjang soybean paste, the stew's savory base

sections.heading: Steps
items: Bring the water or stock to a boil in a small pot over medium-high heat.
Stir in the doenjang until fully dissolved with no lumps.
Add the diced potato first, since it takes longest, and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the onion and zucchini, and simmer another 5 minutes until the potato is fork-tender.
Stir in the garlic and optional gochugaru.
Add the sliced green chili and simmer 2 more minutes.
Gently add the tofu cubes and simmer 2 more minutes, stirring softly.
Taste — it should be savory and earthy. Stir in a little more doenjang if it tastes flat.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle scallion on top, and serve bubbling hot with rice.

recipes.title: Dakgalbi (Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken)
recipes.dish_alt: Spicy red dakgalbi chicken and cabbage in a wide pan
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Cooking Chicken & Vegetables in the Pan
recipes.prep_alt: Marinated chicken, sweet potato, and cabbage cooking together in a wide pan

sections.heading: Steps
items: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, and ginger into a thick red sauce.
Toss the chicken pieces in the sauce and marinate at least 15 minutes, up to an hour.
Heat the sesame oil in a large wide pan over medium heat and cook the sweet potato 3-4 minutes first.
Add the marinated chicken, spreading it out, and let it sear 3 minutes before flipping.
Add the onion and cabbage, and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked through.
If it looks dry before the chicken is done, add a small splash of water.
Stir in the scallion pieces in the last minute of cooking.
Serve straight from the pan, family-style, with rice on the side.

recipes.title: Yangnyeom Chicken (Korean Fried Chicken)
recipes.dish_alt: Crispy Korean fried chicken glazed in glossy red yangnyeom sauce
recipes.prep_alt: Chicken wings frying to a deep golden crisp in hot oil

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the chicken wings completely dry, then toss with salt and pepper.
Coat every piece evenly in the cornstarch and flour mix, shaking off the excess.
Heat about 2 inches of oil to 340°F/170°C in a deep, heavy pot.
Fry the chicken in batches 7-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until light golden and cooked through.
Drain on a wire rack and let the oil come back up to temperature.
Fry all the pieces a second time for 2-3 minutes until deep golden brown and very crunchy.
While the chicken drains, simmer the gochujang, ketchup, honey, soy sauce, and garlic in a pan 1-2 minutes until glossy.
Toss the crispy chicken in the sauce off heat until every piece is coated.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately while hot and crispy.

recipes.title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice Bowl)
recipes.dish_alt: Colorful bibimbap rice bowl with vegetables, beef, and a fried egg
recipes.prep_alt: A sunny-side-up egg frying with a soft runny yolk

sections.heading: Steps
items: Boil the bean sprouts 2-3 minutes until just tender, then scoop out, keeping the water boiling.
Boil the spinach 30 seconds, drain, rinse with cold water, and squeeze out excess water.
Toss the bean sprouts and spinach separately with a pinch of salt, garlic, and sesame oil.
Cook the carrot, zucchini, and shiitake separately, 1-2 minutes each, keeping their colors distinct.
Cook the beef with a splash of soy sauce and garlic 3-4 minutes until fully browned.
Fry the egg sunny-side up until the white sets but the yolk stays runny, about 3 minutes.
Scoop warm rice into each bowl as the base.
Arrange the toppings in separate piles around the rice like a clock face.
Place the fried egg in the center with a spoonful of gochujang beside it.
Drizzle with extra sesame oil and mix everything together just before eating.

recipes.title: Hotteok (Sweet Filled Pancakes, Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Golden-brown hotteok pancakes cut open to show gooey syrup filling
recipes.prep_alt: Sweet cinnamon-brown-sugar filling being wrapped inside soft dough

sections.heading: Steps
items: Stir the warm milk with sugar and yeast, and let it sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in the flour, glutinous rice flour, and salt to form a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and let it rise somewhere warm 45-60 minutes until puffy and doubled.
Mix the brown sugar, cinnamon, and chopped nuts for the filling.
With oiled hands, flatten a golf-ball-size piece of dough in your palm.
Add a spoonful of filling, gather the edges up, and pinch to seal the pouch.
Heat oil in a flat pan over medium heat and place the pouch seam-side down for 1 minute.
Press firmly to flatten into a thick disc, then cook 2-3 minutes until deep golden brown.
Flip and press again lightly, cooking 2-3 minutes more until both sides are golden.
Let it rest 1-2 minutes before serving warm — the filling stays molten hot inside.
